body.name: Destination Job
body.description: On a Sent row (#677), the job the material was sent to; blank on every other row. One record, enforced by the app.

body.name: Destination Address
body.description: On a Sent row (#677), the address the material was sent to, one of Destination Job's; blank on every other row. One record, enforced by the app.

body.name: Send
body.description: On a Received, Send canceled or Written off row (#677), the Sent row whose in-transit quantity it took; blank on a Sent or an Issued row. One record, enforced by the app.

body.name: Material Log (as Destination)
body.description: Reverse link of Material Log."Destination Job" (#677): the Sent rows sending material to this job. The inventory screens read it for what is in transit to the job. Named as this base names a second relation between two tables.

body.name: Material Log (as Destination)
body.description: Reverse link of Material Log."Destination Address" (#677): the Sent rows sending material to this address. Named as this base names a second relation between two tables.

body.name: Material Log (as Send)
body.description: Reverse link of Material Log."Send" (#677): on a Sent row, every Received, Send canceled and Written off row settling it, on whichever job. What is in transit is the Sent row's quantity less theirs (lib/materialTransit.js).

What has happened to a job's material at one of its addresses (#675), append-only: the inventory's ledger. Qty is the change to the stock of Material at Address on Job, so an Issued or a Sent row is negative — but for a Written off row, which moves no address's stock (#677). A delivery is not a row here: the stock at an address is what the deliveries recorded there hold (Delivery Items."Qty") plus the sum of these rows less the Written off ones, computed by lib/materialStock.js and stored nowhere. Material sent between addresses (#677) is a Sent row at the address it left, naming Destination Job and Destination Address; each Received, Send canceled and Written off row names the Sent row it settles in Send, and what is in transit is the Sent row's quantity less theirs, computed by lib/materialTransit.js and stored nowhere.

before: What has happened to a job's material at one of its addresses (#675), append-only: the inventory's ledger. Qty is the change to the stock of Material at Address on Job, so an Issued row is negative. A delivery is not a row here: the stock at an address is what the deliveries recorded there hold (Delivery Items."Qty") plus the sum of these rows, computed by lib/materialStock.js and stored nowhere.

body.description: What happened: Issued (#675) — the site took it from the address to use. Sent (#677) — it left the address for Destination Address on Destination Job; Received — it arrived there; Send canceled — the sender took back what had not arrived; Written off — an admin wrote off what never arrived. Count edited corrects it with a Reason (#678). The screen's words (lib/materialStock.js).

before: What happened: Issued (#675) — the site took it from the address to use. Sent and Received, Send canceled and Written off move it between addresses (#677); Count edited corrects it with a Reason (#678). The screen's words (lib/materialStock.js).

body.description: The change to the stock of Material at Address on Job, in the material's Unit: negative where stock left the address (Issued, Sent), positive where it came in (Received, Send canceled). A WRITTEN OFF ROW IS THE ONE EXCEPTION (#677): it moves no address's stock, since what it writes off left its address with the Sent row and never reached another, so its Qty is what it took out of transit, negative, and the stock leaves it out (lib/materialStock.js) — only what is in transit counts it (lib/materialTransit.js).

before: The change to the stock of Material at Address on Job, in the material's Unit: negative where stock left the address (Issued), positive where it came in.

body.description: The day it happened, as the person recording it gave it — on a Sent row the day it was sent, on a Received row the day it arrived (#677) — not when it was recorded, which is Recorded At. A Send canceled or Written off row holds the day it was recorded, in the recorder's own zone.

before: The day it happened, as the person recording it gave it — not when it was recorded, which is Recorded At.
